questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Vertical pulley pair with landing and slack projectile motion

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational Drill: Vertical pulley pair with landing and slack projectile motion

hints: Apply Newton's second law to the connected stage to find acceleration $a$, use $v^2 = 2as$ to find speed at landing, then use $v^2 = u^2 - 2gh$ with $a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for the slack stage.

walkthrough.text:
Form the equations of motion for particles $A$ and $B$ while the string is taut, and calculate the system acceleration $a$:
$$\text{For } A: \quad T - 2(10) = 2a \implies T - 20 = 2a$$
$$\text{For } B: \quad 3(10) - T = 3a \implies 30 - T = 3a$$
Adding the two equations yields:
$$10 = 5a \implies a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate the speed $v$ of the particles when $B$ has descended $1\text{ m}$ from rest:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as = 0^2 + 2(2)(1) = 4 \implies v = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

After $B$ hits the ground, the string becomes slack ($T = 0$). Particle $A$ moves freely under gravity with initial upward speed $u = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and acceleration $a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Find the additional height $h$ ascended before coming momentarily to rest ($v = 0$):
$$0^2 = 2^2 + 2(-10)h \implies 0 = 4 - 20h \implies h = \frac{4}{20} = 0.2\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
While the string is taut, the two masses move with a shared acceleration driven by the gravitational difference between the two particles:
$$a = \frac{m_B g - m_A g}{m_A + m_B} = \frac{30 - 20}{2 + 3} = \frac{10}{5} = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
$$v = \sqrt{2as} = \sqrt{2(2)(1)} = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

When $B$ hits the ground, do not carry over the old tension. The string goes slack instantly, leaving $A$ moving as an independent projectile under gravity only:
$$v^2 = u^2 - 2gh \implies 0 = 2^2 - 2(10)h \implies h = 0.2\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies Newton's second law to the connected stage ($30 - 20 = 5a$) to obtain $a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and uses $v^2 = 2as$ to find speed $v = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Models particle $A$ in free flight under gravity ($a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$) with $u = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and applies $0 = u^2 - 2gh$ to find additional height $h = 0.2\text{ m}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Rough horizontal surface with slack string deceleration

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational Drill: Rough horizontal surface with slack string deceleration

hints: When the string is slack, tension is zero ($T = 0$). Only limiting friction $F = \mu R$ opposes motion. Use Newton's second law to find deceleration, then apply $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $v = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the normal reaction $R$ and the friction force $F$ acting on block $A$:
$$R = mg = 2(10) = 20\text{ N}$$
$$F = \mu R = 0.3 \times 20 = 6\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law horizontally in the direction of motion, noting that tension is zero ($T = 0$):
$$-F = ma \implies -6 = 2a \implies a = -3\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Thus the deceleration is $3\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Apply the constant acceleration equation with $u = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $v = 0$, and $a = -3\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to find distance $s$:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as \implies 0^2 = 3^2 + 2(-3)s \implies 0 = 9 - 6s \implies s = \frac{9}{6} = 1.5\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Notice that once the string is slack, the tension vanishes completely. The block decelerates purely due to table friction:
$$F = \mu mg = 0.3(2)(10) = 6\text{ N}$$
$$a = -\frac{F}{m} = -\frac{6}{2} = -3\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Use kinematics to find the stopping distance from initial speed $u = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$s = \frac{u^2}{2|a|} = \frac{3^2}{2(3)} = \frac{9}{6} = 1.5\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates friction $F = 0.3 \times 20 = 6\text{ N}$ and uses Newton's second law with $T = 0$ to find deceleration of magnitude $3\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Applies $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $v = 0$ and $u = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find distance $s = 1.5\text{ m}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Smooth inclined plane slack motion

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational Drill: Smooth inclined plane slack motion

hints: With the string slack and no friction, the only force acting along the plane is the component of weight down the plane, giving $a = -g\sin 30^\circ$. Then apply $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces on particle $P$ parallel to the plane in the upward direction, setting $T = 0$:
$$-mg\sin 30^\circ = ma \implies a = -g\sin 30^\circ = -10(0.5) = -5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Thus the particle decelerates at $5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ up the plane.

Apply the kinematic relation $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $v = 0$, and $a = -5\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$0^2 = 4^2 + 2(-5)s \implies 0 = 16 - 10s \implies 10s = 16 \implies s = 1.6\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
On a smooth incline with a slack string, the only opposing force is gravity pulling the particle back down the slope:
$$a = -g\sin\theta = -10\sin 30^\circ = -5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

The particle glides up the incline until all its initial kinetic energy is converted into gravitational potential energy:
$$s = \frac{u^2}{2|a|} = \frac{4^2}{2(5)} = \frac{16}{10} = 1.6\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves weight down the incline with $T = 0$ to find acceleration $a = -g\sin 30^\circ = -5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (or deceleration of magnitude $5\text{ m s}^{-2}$).
Uses $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $v = 0$ and $u = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to obtain distance $s = 1.6\text{ m}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Boundary obstacle check comparing height with ceiling

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational Drill: Boundary obstacle check comparing height with ceiling

hints: Calculate the maximum unrestricted height $h = \frac{u^2}{2g}$. If $h \ge 1.2\text{ m}$, the particle reaches the ceiling; then find its speed at $s = 1.2\text{ m}$ using $v^2 = u^2 - 2gs$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the unrestricted maximum height $h$ that particle $A$ would reach moving freely under gravity ($a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$) before coming to instantaneous rest ($v = 0$):
$$v^2 = u^2 - 2gh \implies 0 = 5^2 - 2(10)h \implies 20h = 25 \implies h = 1.25\text{ m}$$
Since $1.25\text{ m} > 1.2\text{ m}$, the particle reaches the ceiling before coming to rest.

Find the speed $v$ of particle $A$ at displacement $s = 1.2\text{ m}$:
$$v^2 = u^2 - 2gs = 5^2 - 2(10)(1.2) = 25 - 24 = 1 \implies v = \sqrt{1} = 1\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Always check whether the trajectory reaches a physical boundary before stopping:
$$h_{\text{stop}} = \frac{u^2}{2g} = \frac{25}{20} = 1.25\text{ m}$$
Since the ceiling is at $1.2\text{ m} < 1.25\text{ m}$, the particle collides with the ceiling while still moving upwards.

Now compute the impact velocity at the ceiling:
$$v = \sqrt{u^2 - 2gs} = \sqrt{25 - 20(1.2)} = \sqrt{1} = 1\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates unrestricted maximum height $h = \frac{u^2}{2g} = 1.25\text{ m}$ and deduces that particle $A$ reaches the ceiling because $1.25 > 1.2$.
Applies $v^2 = u^2 - 2gs$ with $s = 1.2\text{ m}$ to obtain impact speed $v = 1\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Time until slack string becomes taut again

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational Drill: Time until slack string becomes taut again

hints: Because the surface is smooth and the string is slack, both velocities remain constant. The rate of separation is $v_A + v_B$, and the string becomes taut when separation equals $2.5\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Express the positions of $A$ and $B$ relative to an origin at $A$'s initial position taking rightwards as positive:
$$x_A(t) = -1.2t$$
$$x_B(t) = 1.0 + 1.8t$$
The separation of the particles at time $t$ is:
$$\text{Separation} = x_B(t) - x_A(t) = (1.0 + 1.8t) - (-1.2t) = 1.0 + 3.0t$$

The string becomes taut when the separation reaches the string length of $2.5\text{ m}$:
$$1.0 + 3.0t = 2.5 \implies 3.0t = 1.5 \implies t = \frac{1.5}{3.0} = 0.5\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
The particles move in opposite directions, so their relative speed of separation is the sum of their individual speeds:
$$v_{\text{sep}} = 1.2 + 1.8 = 3.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$\text{Separation}(t) = 1.0 + 3.0t$$

The string must unfold by an additional $2.5 - 1.0 = 1.5\text{ m}$ before snapping taut:
$$t = \frac{2.5 - 1.0}{3.0} = \frac{1.5}{3.0} = 0.5\text{ s}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Forms the separation expression $1.0 + (1.2 + 1.8)t = 1.0 + 3.0t$ and sets it equal to the string length $2.5\text{ m}$.
Solves $1.0 + 3.0t = 2.5$ to obtain time $t = 0.5\text{ s}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Vertical particle return time to transition level

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational Drill: Vertical particle return time to transition level

hints: At the highest point, vertical velocity is zero ($v = 0$). Use $v = u - gt$. By symmetry of free vertical motion, the return time is double the time to the highest point.

walkthrough.text:
Use the equation $v = u + at$ with upward positive, $u = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $v = 0$ at the highest point:
$$0 = 3 - 10t_1 \implies 10t_1 = 3 \implies t_1 = 0.3\text{ s}$$

Set vertical displacement $s = 0$ to find the total time $T$ until returning to the initial level:
$$s = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 \implies 0 = 3T - 5T^2 \implies T(3 - 5T) = 0$$
Since $T > 0$, we find:
$$T = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6\text{ s}$$
(Equivalently, by symmetry: $T = 2t_1 = 2 \times 0.3 = 0.6\text{ s}$.)

teacher_walkthrough.text:
When moving freely under gravity, upward deceleration is simply $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$. The time to shed all upward speed is:
$$t_{\text{peak}} = \frac{u}{g} = \frac{3}{10} = 0.3\text{ s}$$

Because the path is completely symmetric under uniform gravity without resistance, descending back to the transition level takes the exact same time:
$$t_{\text{total}} = 2 t_{\text{peak}} = 2(0.3) = 0.6\text{ s}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses $v = u - gt$ with $v = 0$ and $u = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find time to highest point $t = 0.3\text{ s}$.
Applies symmetry ($2 \times 0.3\text{ s}$) or solves $s = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = 0$ to find total time $t = 0.6\text{ s}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Easy: Complete vertical pulley two-stage problem with landing and greatest height

hints: Write Newton's second law for $A$ moving upwards ($T - 10 = 1a$) and $B$ moving downwards ($30 - T = 3a$), then solve simultaneously for $a$ and $T$.

walkthrough.text:
Write the equations of motion for particles $A$ and $B$:
$$\text{For } A \text{ (upwards)}: \quad T - m_A g = m_A a \implies T - 1(10) = 1a \implies T - 10 = a$$
$$\text{For } B \text{ (downwards)}: \quad m_B g - T = m_B a \implies 3(10) - T = 3a \implies 30 - T = 3a$$

Add the two equations to eliminate $T$ and solve for $a$, then find $T$:
$$(T - 10) + (30 - T) = a + 3a \implies 20 = 4a \implies a = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
$$T = 10 + a = 10 + 5 = 15\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
For a simple vertical pair over a smooth pulley, total driving force is the difference in weight, acting on the sum of the masses:
$$a = \frac{m_B g - m_A g}{m_A + m_B} = \frac{30 - 10}{1 + 3} = \frac{20}{4} = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute the acceleration into either particle's equation to obtain string tension:
$$T = m_A(g + a) = 1(10 + 5) = 15\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Forms equations of motion $T - 10 = a$ and $30 - T = 3a$ and solves to find acceleration $a = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Substitutes $a = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into either equation of motion to find tension $T = 15\text{ N}$.
